h: The great rescue from the Falklands
p: The ship you see today very nearly didn't make it home. After her passenger days, the SS Great Britain was turned into a sailing cargo ship and ended up in the Falkland Islands, used as a storage hulk. In 1937 she was scuttled in a bay near Port Stanley and left to rot.

Then, in 1970, came one of the great salvage stories. She was floated onto a pontoon and towed thousands of miles across the Atlantic back to Bristol. She came back into the very dock where she was built on 19 July 1970, exactly 127 years to the day after her launch. Goosebumps.
Keep that story in mind as you walk round and you'll see the ship in a whole new light: every rivet has been on one heck of a journey.

For timing, allow at least half a day. Families with younger kids might want to split it with lunch at Wapping Wharf nearby, where there's a cluster of independent food spots. The M Shed museum, all about Bristol's history and people, is a short walk along the harbour and pairs up brilliantly.
